questions.question: A feature distribution changes, but no outcomes have arrived yet. What can the team conclude?
options: The model must be retrained immediately
P(Y|X) definitely changed
An input shift occurred, but model harm and concept drift are not yet established
The alert is necessarily a data-quality defect
questions.explanation: Unlabeled feature movement is evidence about P(X). Labels or other outcome evidence are needed to establish harm or changed P(Y|X).

questions.question: Which evidence most strongly supports a data-quality incident rather than a population shift?
options: A feature exceeds its unit contract by 1,000x exactly when an upstream release starts
A known seasonal segment grows gradually
The positive class becomes more common
A domain classifier distinguishes two valid device populations
questions.explanation: A contract violation aligned with an upstream release identifies a broken measurement mechanism that should be repaired before model adaptation.

questions.question: Why can a tiny distribution difference produce frequent alerts on very large samples?
options: Large samples always corrupt feature values
Statistical power can make small effects significant
KS distance grows automatically with sample count
Labels become unavailable at scale
questions.explanation: Hypothesis tests become sensitive to smaller effects as sample size grows, so alerting must include magnitude, uncertainty, and operational materiality.

questions.question: Confirmed outcome prevalence changes while within-class score shapes and ranking stay stable. Which response is the best first candidate?
options: Repair an unbroken schema
Retrain automatically on every recent record
Evaluate recalibration or a decision-threshold change
Ignore the labels and monitor only inputs
questions.explanation: This evidence supports prior probability shift with useful ranking preserved, making policy recalibration a narrower candidate than relearning the model.

questions.question: Severe user harm is reported, but labeled evidence is sparse and the cause is uncertain. What should the operational boundary prioritize?
options: Contain exposure with a fallback or rollback while collecting evidence
Promote a newly trained model without evaluation
Move the reference window so the alert disappears
Wait without changing traffic because labels are incomplete
questions.explanation: High potential harm can justify a reversible containment action even when evidence is not mature enough to authorize retraining.

questions.question: What is the strongest release evidence after retraining for concept drift?
options: The model artifact has a newer timestamp
The drift detector no longer fires on training data
The candidate recovers the affected slice, protects historical slices, and holds in a live canary
The training loss is lower than before
questions.explanation: Recovery requires current-slice improvement, regression protection, and controlled live evidence with a rollback boundary.
